## Proof

**Claim.** The Lebesgue measure (i.e. $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure) of the boundary $\partial\Omega$ of a bounded Lipschitz domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is zero:

$$m_n(\partial\Omega)=0.$$

**Definition.** A bounded open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is a *Lipschitz domain* (has Lipschitz boundary) if for every point $x_0\in\partial\Omega$ there exist a neighborhood $U_{x_0}$ of $x_0$, a rotation $R$, and a Lipschitz function $f:\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ with Lipschitz constant $L$, such that, writing coordinates as $(y',y_n)$ with $y'\in\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$,

$$\Omega\cap U_{x_0}=\{(y',y_n)\in U_{x_0}: y_n < f(y')\},\qquad \partial\Omega\cap U_{x_0}=\{(y',y_n)\in U_{x_0}: y_n=f(y')\}.$$

That is, locally the boundary is the graph of a Lipschitz function of $n-1$ variables.

**Key lemma.** *The graph of any Lipschitz function $g:\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ has $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero.*

*Proof of lemma.* Let $g:\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\to\mathbb{R}$ be Lipschitz with constant $L$. It suffices to show that $g$ restricted to any bounded cube $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ has a graph of measure zero, since $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ is a countable union of such cubes.

Fix a bounded cube $Q$ of side length $s$. Partition $Q$ into $N^{n-1}$ sub-cubes $Q_j$ of side length $s/N$. On each $Q_j$, the oscillation of $g$ is at most $L\sqrt{n-1}\,s/N$, so the graph $\Gamma_g\cap(Q_j\times\mathbb{R})$ is contained in a rectangular box of dimensions

$$\underbrace{(s/N)\times\cdots\times(s/N)}_{n-1}\times \bigl(2L\sqrt{n-1}\,s/N\bigr),$$

which has $n$-volume

$$\left(\frac{s}{N}\right)^{n-1}\cdot \frac{2L\sqrt{n-1}\,s}{N}=\frac{2L\sqrt{n-1}\,s^{n}}{N^{n}}.$$

Summing over all $N^{n-1}$ sub-cubes,

$$m_n^*(\Gamma_g\cap(Q\times\mathbb{R}))\le N^{n-1}\cdot \frac{2L\sqrt{n-1}\,s^{n}}{N^{n}}=\frac{2L\sqrt{n-1}\,s^{n}}{N}.$$

Letting $N\to\infty$, the outer measure is $0$. Hence $m_n(\Gamma_g\cap(Q\times\mathbb{R}))=0$. Taking a countable union over cubes covering $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$ gives $m_n(\Gamma_g)=0$. $\square$

**Completing the proof.** Since $\Omega$ is bounded, $\partial\Omega$ is compact. By the Lipschitz boundary property, every $x_0\in\partial\Omega$ has a neighborhood $U_{x_0}$ in which $\partial\Omega$ coincides with the graph of a Lipschitz function (after a rotation, which preserves Lebesgue measure). By compactness, finitely many such neighborhoods $U_{x_1},\dots,U_{x_k}$ cover $\partial\Omega$. Therefore

$$\partial\Omega\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}\bigl(\partial\Omega\cap U_{x_i}\bigr)=\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}\Gamma_{f_i}\cap U_{x_i},$$

where each $\Gamma_{f_i}$ is the graph of a Lipschitz function. By the lemma, each $\Gamma_{f_i}$ has $n$-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero, hence each $\Gamma_{f_i}\cap U_{x_i}$ has measure zero. By subadditivity,

$$m_n(\partial\Omega)\le\sum_{i=1}^{k}m_n(\Gamma_{f_i}\cap U_{x_i})=0.$$

Since measure is non-negative, $m_n(\partial\Omega)=0$.

**Conclusion.** The Lebesgue measure of the boundary of a bounded Lipschitz domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is

$$\boxed{0}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
